findings.issue: The SET NX key limits notices per owner, but nothing limits them per requester. One signed-in account can go through numbers every 30 s (about 2,880 a day) and cause one PHONE_CLAIM_ATTEMPT email to each distinct verified owner it hits. The attacker learns nothing from this, and each victim gets at most one email a day. It is still a cheap way to send mass mail from our domain, which can hurt sender reputation, and when self-registration is on, extra accounts multiply it.
findings.fix: Follow-up in F-06 scope: add a per-requester daily cap on claim notices or on add-phone calls (for example a SharedWindowCounter on requesterId). The response for the caller must stay unchanged so it does not become an oracle.

findings.issue: SMS pumping (the F-06 finding) is neither better nor worse after this diff. The old code also sent no SMS for a taken number, because it threw 409 first. Free numbers still have only the 30 s per-user cooldown, with no per-phone or daily cap. Design section 5 says 'this change cuts it', which is wrong and could lead someone to close the F-06 item.
findings.fix: Correct the design and risk text to say SMS exposure is unchanged, and keep the per-phone and daily SMS caps tracked under F-06 (TD-P6-11).

findings.issue: PASSWORD_SET goes to the same mailbox that received the reset link. If that mailbox is compromised (for example a non-Gmail address on a Google-only account), the attacker gets a lasting password credential and can delete the notice. The alert helps only when the real owner sees the mail first. ADR 0007 accepts this residual risk under AC-12(b). No new takeover path is added: reset already required mailbox control and already created the credential.
findings.fix: Optional hardening: show 'password set on <date>' in /account/security, or put a login alert on the first password login after a PASSWORD_SET, so the owner gets a signal outside the mailbox.

findings.issue: If Redis hangs instead of refusing connections, each notifier task blocks up to the Lettuce default command timeout of 60 s. The virtual-thread executor has no bound, so tasks pile up during an outage. The per-user cooldown limits the build-up and nothing reaches the request path, so this is only resource hygiene.
findings.fix: Set a short Redis command timeout (spring.data.redis.timeout, for example 2 s), or use a bounded executor for the notifier.

summary: Enumeration is closed on the add, resend and verify paths. For a taken and a free number, add-phone runs the same DB work: the existence check runs in both cases, then changePhone, then issueCode with the same per-user 30 s cooldown. Both return 202 with an empty body. The only difference is the last step, and both versions just hand a task to a virtual-thread executor (NotificationGateway.sendSms is async too), so request timing matches. A resend inside the cooldown returns the same 429 AUTH_RATE_LIMITED for both. On verify, a lost race, a unique-index violation and a guessed decoy code all return the same exception and detail as a wrong code (401 AUTH_OTP_INVALID). A correct decoy guess also gets 401, so guessing teaches the attacker nothing. AUTH_PHONE_TAKEN is no longer emitted anywhere. Two accounts still cannot both verify one number. The code is consumed in its own transaction, then the in-transaction re-check runs, and the partial unique index users_phone_verified_key backs it up. Tests cover the lost race and the index. The owner notice has a hard bound of one email per owner per window, using an atomic SET NX PX keyed on the owner UUID with no phone number in Redis. If Redis fails, the notice is skipped (fail-closed) with a throttled WARN and no exception. Twenty concurrent attempts produced exactly one email in the test. The reset path keeps its existing behaviour, creating a credential for passwordless accounts. It now sends PASSWORD_SET to the account address after commit; the send fails open, the email contains no secrets, and HTML escaping is tested. No new takeover path: the reset link already went to that mailbox. PII: logs contain only userId and exception class names. The owner email shows only the last 4 digits and names nobody. The ADR sets the deploy order: notification-service first. Endpoint auth is unchanged (signed-in /me routes), and the diff adds no new dependencies. SMS pumping exposure is unchanged, not reduced as the design claims. The remaining items are minor: no per-requester cap on notice emails, the inaccurate SMS-cost statement, the residual risk of the same-mailbox PASSWORD_SET, and the Redis timeout. Approve.
